The user interface for this device consists of a select button, a set button, and an LCD module. The select and set buttons are used to choose skin type and sun protection factor (SPF) from a pre-set list and allow resetting of the device. The LCD module simultaneously displays the instantaneous UV exposure, the accumulated UV dosage, the total UV exposure time, the selected skin type, and the selected SPF. The device is designed to use the selected skin type and SPF to calculate the user’s personal UV exposure. This provides the user with continuous feedback of his/her UV exposure. It also alerts the user when the accumulated UV exposure begins to reach potentially harmful levels.
V. Discussion

While our prototype GaN UV detector functions according to our initial specifications, it could still benefit from further improvement. Specifically, by incorporating aluminum into the GaN photodetector structure, it is theoretically possible to grow a UV photodetector which has a much higher correlation with the erythemal weighting function. In addition, the options for skin type and SPF in our prototype are extremely limited; the skin’s sensitivity to UV radiation needs to be more

accurately modeled to take into consideration variances based on a wider number of skin types and SPF’s. Finally, the device must have reduced size, weight, and power consumption to be feasible for commercial use. At present, the whole unit measures ~15 x 10 x 3 cm; ideally the device could be made small enough to fit in a watch or cellphone.
VI. Summary and Conclusion

Steadily increasing rates of skin cancer due to prolonged exposure to solar UV radiation indicate the need for personal UV exposure monitoring. In this paper, we have reported the development of a compact prototype GaN based p-i-n UV photodetector unit which provides a convenient way to monitor personal UV exposure. Our research has covered all aspects of this device from the fabrication of the semiconductor photodetector to the accompanying electronics and associated software. It appears possible that our technology could be commercialized, thereby providing a means to reliably prevent UV overexposure and consequently to reduce the incidence of skin cancer among the general population.
